methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Site-by-site monthly FCFF from 1-Jul-2026 (100-yr horizon, repeating refresh cycles, g=0), one row per inventory site (src36). Contracted: Microsoft Horizons 1-4 200MW IT at $9.7m/MW-yr ($1.94bn), H1 from Aug-26, H2-4 from Jan-27, 5 yrs, $4.36bn GPU + $1.0bn DC left to spend, $0.93bn prepayment still to receive, $1.94bn credited yrs 3-5; Prince George ~28MW IT, $0.5bn ARR (60% expiring Dec-27, GB300 hall 3 yrs); Mackenzie ~44MW IT and Childress 2026 ~28MW IT sharing $1.56bn ARR, 3 yrs, $3.5bn B300 GPU capex, 50% prepaid; NVIDIA ~60MW gross / ~43MW IT, $0.68bn ARR, 5 yrs from Mar-27, $1.6bn Dell. Under construction, uncontracted (probability on schedule, else 24-month delay; DC capex committed either way): Childress 190MW gross/136 IT (0.85), Horizons 5-6 100 IT (0.75), Canal Flats ~21 IT (0.80), Sweetwater 1 phase 1 200 IT (0.70), all at $20.6m/MW-yr 3-yr terms, GPU $45m/MW (2.2x ARR), 45% prepaid. Pipeline S11-S16 (2.9GW IT): build NPV at WACC is negative for every site (-$0.01bn to -$0.93bn), so each is carried at its power-rights value ($0.05-0.30m/gross MW) instead. GPU life (round-3 method): contract price for the term, then re-lease = min(1, spot index/contract share of launch spot) x 0.85; value-maximising refresh capped at 7 yrs: 6 yrs market-priced, 7 yrs Microsoft/NVIDIA; refreshed capacity re-contracts at market ($20.6m/MW, $45m/MW GPU, no prepayment); salvage 8%/6% at 6/7 yrs. Costs: $1.6m/MW-yr direct, 8% variable, 2%/yr repairs after yr 3, $0.75m/MW-yr DC maintenance, $1.5bn corporate (PV -$13.8bn). Discounting: contract-term cash flows at 7.0% (Microsoft), 7.5% (NVIDIA), 10.0% (non-IG AI developers); everything else 11% WACC. Equity = site PVs $11.3bn + rights $0.4bn + mining $0.1bn - corporate $13.8bn + net cash $0.78bn = -$1.16bn / 452M x 1.195 = -$3.1 (single 11%: -$1.38bn, -$3.7). Sensitivities (split): uniform 5y -$6.3, 7y -$0.7; GPU $40m/MW +$21.3, $36m/MW +$46.8, $50m/MW -$15.4; glut 1.0 +$15.6, 0.70 -$14.2; WACC 10% +$2.2 / 12% -$6.4; corporate $1.0bn about +$9.5; contracted rates 6/6.5/9% -$2.3.

bull.story: 2027 capacity contracts at ~$25m/MW (GPU capex/ARR nearer 1.9x than 2.2x: DCF ~+$20), Sweetwater/Kiowa tenants signed, rents stay firm (no glut haircut: DCF ~+$16), IG-style financing extends to NVIDIA and new contracts; 9-10x on ~$6.5bn+ NTM EBITDA.

thesis_break_reason: Kept at the supervisor's $21: diluted market cap ~$9.5bn (452M sh), EV ~2.2x the ~$4.7bn contracted ARR (2026 program ~$4bn + NVIDIA ~$0.7bn), ~27% below the $28.93 52-week low. The stock fell 57% June-July 2026 without a fundamental break, so mid-$20s is sentiment range. My DCF is now about -$3 (site-by-site, split rate), so $21 is a market-behaviour test, not a valuation floor: trading below it would most likely mean failed or distressed FY27 funding, a Microsoft Horizon miss beyond the Q2-2027 grace period, a non-IG customer default on 2026 capacity, or a visible collapse in GPU re-leasing rates.

reasoning: Round 4 (sites and split discounting). I rebuilt the DCF as a monthly site-by-site model on the checked inventory (src36), one row per site. Fixed flag F02: NVIDIA (~60MW gross, $0.68bn ARR, 5 yrs) is its own early-2027 cohort, and 2026 non-Microsoft capacity is ~100MW IT at $2.06bn ARR. Fixed F08: the $2.1bn '4.2GW x $0.5m' land figure is gone; each pipeline site has a build NPV (negative at 11% for all six) and is carried at its rights value ($0.4bn total). F09 (undisclosed BC 2027 headroom MW) and F10 (mining residual, +$0.1bn) are addressed; F11 (Microsoft prepayment attribution) is handled by explicit prepayment receipts and credits, which replace round 3's 'deferred at face' and '+$2.0bn float' judgment items. I also brought new-build GPU capex into line with IREN's own orders (2.2x ARR, from 1.73x), cut salvage per the supervisor, re-ran the value-maximising refresh (now 6 yrs for market cohorts, 7 for Microsoft/NVIDIA, capped at the 7-yr physical evidence), and let refreshed capacity re-contract at market terms. Split discounting at 7.0/7.5/10% on contract-term cash flows (anchored on the 6.00% A-rated Microsoft facility and the 9.0% Mackenzie paper, both checked against primary text) moves the DCF only from -$3.7 to -$3.1: within each contract, receipts are largely spent on the GPUs and data centers that earn them, so a lower rate on that bundle barely changes its PV. Value comes from post-contract and refresh cash flows, which stay at 11%. The DCF is dominated by GPU capex per dollar of ARR (1.95x gives +$21) and re-lease prices (no haircut +$16). Blend 40/60 with the unchanged $36 multiple = $20.4 (from $23.6). The 12-month price is set by funding, Horizon/NVIDIA delivery and how the market capitalises contracted EBITDA, so I shift the distribution down only ~3% (median ~$32.7 from ~$33). Scenarios $16/$34/$70 (mean ~$37). Thesis break $21 kept. 1-month ladder unchanged. Research this round: two WebFetches of company releases plus a grep of the downloaded 10-K text to verify the financing anchors; no searches. Site facts are company-sourced (allowed for basic facts), which lowers this round's in-lane share.

discounting.contracted_rate: 7.0% Microsoft (S01); 7.5% NVIDIA (S03); 10.0% non-IG AI developers (S02, S07, S08); contract-term cash flows only, including the initial capex and prepayments they carry
discounting.basis: Microsoft: the A-rated (Fitch A / DBRS A(low)) secured facility against these GPUs and cash flows prices at 6.00% blended (USPP SOFR+2.13%, DDTL SOFR+2.25%), verified in the 1-Jun-2026 release; +1pt for completion of H2-4, SLA/operating risk and the equity slice behind 96% funding. NVIDIA (S&P AA): no financing closed yet and commissioning still ahead, so +0.5pt over Microsoft. Non-IG (Perplexity, Together AI, Fluidstack and others): the Mackenzie notes/MFSA cost 9.0% fixed, 30-month amortising, 90% of GPU capex, parent-guaranteed (10-K text verified); unhedged residual counterparty risk puts the equity rate at 10%, between that and the 11% WACC. Post-contract, refresh, uncontracted, pipeline and terminal cash flows and corporate costs not allocated to contracts at 11%. Corporate cost is allocated to streams by revenue and discounted with them. Effect is small (+$0.22bn, +$0.6/share) because contract-term cash flows net to about -$4.2bn after the GPU and DC capex that earns them; the rate on post-contract cash flows drives value. Both use the same x1.195 roll-forward to Oct-2027.
